title: Second-column fixations and F-pattern in text-page eyetracking
statement:
In an eyetracking study of text web pages, information in a second column received more fixations than the same information lower in a single column, and the F-pattern appeared in the left column but not the right, so a right-hand column can lift secondary content into view but should not be expected to be scanned like the main column.

Options:
- Single column: Single-column long text with clear headings (simple, mobile-friendly) (fits: editorial, calm, simple)
- Main plus supporting column: Two columns with the main story on the left and supporting facts or proof in a second column kept in view (fits: informational, professional, organized)
- Self-contained columns: Two self-contained columns, each with its own heading (for example a comparison), so neither depends on being scanned like the other (fits: technical, clear, modern)
- No ad neighbours: Keep ads or promotional blocks out of columns that carry key content, since browsing viewers looked at ads more than searching viewers (fits: trustworthy, editorial)
appliesWhen: Applies to: media publishing. Audience: general.

source.title: Eye Movements on a Single-Column and Double-Column Text Web Page
source.authors: Sav Shrestha; Justin Owens; Barbara S. Chaparro
source.venue: 52nd Annual Meeting of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society (HFES), New York
